          "statement": "Inputs are an order $d\\ge0$ real or complex Schur matrix $T$, or a regular real or complex generalized Schur pair $(S,T)$, with the declared diagonal block partition. For rational or dyadic arrays, the exact core uses rational arithmetic and positive square roots, with exact real-algebraic sign comparisons where needed. Exact decisions on arbitrary real inputs are an exact-real arithmetic model, not a bit-computability claim. The bounded-evaluator branch returns arithmetic-inconclusive whenever a needed zero, sign, division, or normalization remains unresolved.\n\n1. Validate dimensions, the declared block pattern, and regularity of each generalized diagonal pair in one finite scan. For ordinary scalar blocks over either field classify $t_{ii}$ by $\\operatorname{Re}t_{ii}<0$ or $>0$ for CARE; for real $2\\times2$ blocks first verify negative discriminant and then classify by trace less than or greater than zero. Exact equality with the selected boundary returns boundary-spectrum. A bounded enclosure touching the boundary returns separation-inconclusive. Require that the selected block sizes sum to $r$, or return dimension-mismatch. Invalid patterns or singular local homogeneous pairs return invalid-form. Compute the initial inversion count once by scanning all ordered block pairs after classification.\n\n2. Give every whole block its selected or complementary label. Locate the leftmost adjacent complementary-selected inversion. If none exists, return ordered with the current exact arrays and accumulated factors. If an inversion exists but $K$ swap attempts have already been made, return swap-budget-exhausted. Otherwise consume one attempt before starting its local construction. Let $p,q\\in\\{1,2\\}$ be the two adjacent block sizes (over $\\mathbb C$, $p=q=1$), with local blocks\n$$T_{JJ}=\\begin{bmatrix}A&C\\\\0&B\\end{bmatrix}$$\nfor ordinary Schur form, or\n$$S_{JJ}=\\begin{bmatrix}A&C\\\\0&B\\end{bmatrix},\\qquad T_{JJ}=\\begin{bmatrix}D&F\\\\0&E\\end{bmatrix}$$\nfor QZ form. With column-vectorization, form the local coefficient system\n$$H=I_q\\otimes A-B^T\\otimes I_p,\\qquad h=-\\operatorname{vec}(C)$$\nfor ordinary Schur, with unknown $\\operatorname{vec}(R)$, and\n$$H=\\begin{bmatrix}I_q\\otimes A&-B^T\\otimes I_p\\\\I_q\\otimes D&-E^T\\otimes I_p\\end{bmatrix},\\qquad h=-\\begin{bmatrix}\\operatorname{vec}(C)\\\\\\operatorname{vec}(F)\\end{bmatrix}$$\nfor QZ, with unknown $[\\operatorname{vec}(R);\\operatorname{vec}(L)]$. Solve $Hx=h$ and $HY=I$ by finite Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting: at each stage scan the finite remaining submatrix, choose an entry of largest certified modulus with lexicographic ties, swap rows and columns, eliminate, and back-substitute while undoing column permutations. An exact all-zero remaining submatrix returns swap-singular. An unresolved pivot or range failure returns separation-inconclusive or range-failure. Verify $Hx=h$ and $HY=I$ exactly, or verify a usable approximate-inverse certificate $\\|I-YH\\|_2\\le\\theta<1$ and still solve $Hx=h$ exactly. In the latter case it gives $\\|H^{-1}\\|_2\\le\\|Y\\|_2/(1-\\theta)$. In the exact-inverse branch take $\\beta=\\|Y\\|_F$ in exact arithmetic, or an outward upper bound for that norm; in the approximate-inverse branch take an outward bound for $\\|Y\\|_2/(1-\\theta)$. Require $\\eta\\beta\\le1$; otherwise return swap-separation-inconclusive. Record the threshold, solves, pivot decisions and certificate.\n\n4. For ordinary Schur form set $V=[R;I_q]$. For QZ set $V=[R;I_q]$ and $W_L=[L;I_q]$.           "statement": "Let $F\\in\\{\\mathbb R,\\mathbb C\\}$, $A\\in F^{n\\times n}$, $B\\in F^{n\\times m}$, $C\\in F^{p\\times n}$, and $R=R^*\\in F^{m\\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\\|L^{-1}B^*v\\|_2^2\\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\\|Cv\\|_2^2\\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\\mathbb C$.\n\nThe **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is\n$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$\nIts residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.\n\nFor $X=X^*\\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because\n$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete\nalgebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is\n$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$\nIts residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are\n$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$\nA CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.\n\nFor Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives\n$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$\nIn either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is\n$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because\n$S_X=R+B^*XB$.
